text:
Ty Dellandrea's most noticed moment lately came with his gloves off. Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest posted "Dellandrea and Peeke drop em now. Fans getting their money's worth tonight" during San Jose's latest game, which fits the role: a checking forward with 39 hits and 13 blocked shots in 14 games, playing a little over 12 minutes a night.

The offense has not come. He has two assists and no goals, 12 shots without one going in, and only 0.73 expected goals (the quality of his chances). Some of that is bad luck, since the Sharks have scored less than their chances suggest with him on the ice, but the process is thin too: at five on five San Jose has taken 38% of the expected goals with him out there, about six points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey had a similar story last season, around replacement level with the team creating less offense when he played. The 13th pick of the 2018 draft is 26 now, and our range for his full season sits at 3 to 11 goals. For now his value is in the hits, the matchups and the odd fight.
headline: Ty Dellandrea is still waiting on his first goal
